phase_name: Permission Broker Foundation Policy Applicability Contract Independent Verification
summary: Independent-verification phase (no src/pcae/** file modified, confirmed via git diff --name-only 234fce06..HEAD -- src/pcae/, empty; no runtime-capability change, confirmed via pcae runtime inspect before/after: Observed / observe / unavailable, unchanged). Independently re-derived PBPA-001 v1.0 from primary source rather than trusting Phase 148C.3's own text. Re-confirmed contract identity (114 unique PBPA-REQ-### requirements, no gaps/duplicates, no competing applicability authority in docs/contracts/); the applicability/evaluation separation is genuine and non-invertible (direct inspection of MissingHumanApprovalRule.evaluate(), which reads only approval_present); the per-policy APPLICABLE/NOT_APPLICABLE result model introduces no fourth broker-level decision value (DECISION_VALUES confirmed exactly (ALLOW, DENY, HUMAN_REVIEW)); the hybrid metadata+predicate architecture concentrates applicability authority in the Foundation, never the caller (no exclude_policies-shaped parameter exists anywhere in the request/broker/registry API); and independently re-derived all twelve POL-001..012 applicability rows from primary source, finding no discrepancy with PBPA-001's own matrix. Performed the specific adversarial re-examination PBPA-001 Section 43 required of POL-004's scope: traced an apparent textual collision between INV-003's verbatim 'mutating execution' and the request model's execution_class="mutation" value through three independent, B-1-predating primary sources (the PR-compatible workflow's Git Approval / Execution Approval separation, the Phase 109 command-category table, and NG-008's own execution-readiness-lifecycle scope statement) and confirmed the two concepts are distinct -- POL-004's frozen scope ({shell, backend, adapter, rollback}) is independently re-derivable, not merely ratified. Empirically exercised the live, unmodified Foundation for four representative request shapes, confirming B-1 is real and reproducible today (push-shaped and shell-shaped requests both reach HUMAN_REVIEW via POL-004 identically, pre-applicability). Adversarially tested every fail-closed attack surface this phase could construct (unknown/missing/future execution_class, applicability-predicate failure, missing/duplicate policy, empty applicable set, caller-supplied exclusion) and found a specified, fail-closed defense for each. Recorded two Non-Blocking findings not present in PBPA-001's own findings table: V-1, a terminology hazard (the 'mutation' collision between INV-003 and execution_class, resolved but recommended for future disambiguation) and V-2, a textual gap (the empty-applicable-set case is not reachable under the current matrix but lacks an explicit contract statement). Verdict: VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- POLICY APPLICABILITY IMPLEMENTATION PLANNING MAY PROCEED. Does not close B-1 -- Finding B-1 remains explicitly OPEN; does not authorize implementation; does not begin 148D. See docs/verification/PHASE_148C.4_PERMISSION_BROKER_FOUNDATION_POLICY_APPLICABILITY_CONTRACT_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION.md for full detail.
tests_added_or_updated: No new test file added -- this phase is a verification-only phase per its No-Go Boundary; no production code path changed, so there is no new production behavior to test. The existing Permission Broker Foundation test suites (tests/test_permission_broker_foundation.py, tests/test_permission_broker_policy_composition_hardening.py, tests/test_permission_broker_policy_rule_framework.py, 171 tests) were re-run live and passed cleanly. The fast_green marker suite (this repository's documented regression-check suite) was re-run live: 4390 passed, 1 failed, 105 warnings in 118.09s; the single failure (tests/test_backend_cli.py::TestBackendReviewCreate::test_create_persists_to_latest) was independently re-run in isolation and passed in 0.60s, confirming a parallelization-order flake unrelated to this phase (no src/pcae/** file touched; the failing test's feature area, backend review persistence, has no relationship to Permission Broker Foundation).
